newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan power plant to offer shares to public.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan power plant to offer shares to public.

text.p: Pakistan's private Japan Power Generation Ltd, which is building a 120-megawatt power plant, will launch 13.8 million 10-rupee shares to the public next month, a company director said on Wednesday.

Asad Ali Uppal told Reuters the company had sought permission from the government's Corporate Law Authority (CLA) for the public offering after getting approval from the Karachi Stock Exchange for the issue of shares in October.

He said the company had already placed 135 million rupees worth of shares with individuals, firms and associates in July and $25 million were placed overseas in March through the Bahrain-based Islamic Investment Company of the Gulf.
Last September, it had completed the process of securing finances for the $123 million project at Raiwand, near the Punjab province capital of Lahore, which is to come on stream in early 1997.

The electricity generated by the plant will be bought by the state-owned Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) at the rate of 6.5 U.S. cents per kilowatt hour under an agreement signed between the two sides in March 1995.
Japan Power has an agreement with Toyota Tsusho Corp of Japan for a supplier's credit of $82 million.
